For 10 points each, answer these questions about ores.
Pyrite, goethite, magnetite, and hematite are ores of this transition metal element, whose oxide is called "rust".

This black, amorphous ore, a form of uraninite, contains uranium oxide, as well as small amounts of radium from the decay of uranium. Uranium, radium, and polonium were all first discovered in this ore, and it can be processed into yellowcake through leaching methods.

Bauxite, an aluminum ore, is processed into alumina in the Bayer process, which is then processed into aluminum metal in this process named after an American and a Frenchman. The alumina is dissolved in a carbon-lined bath of molten cryolite, then electrolyzed.
Answer the following about an American art movement for 10 points each.
Paintings from this movement frequently depicted the Catskill and Adirondack Mountains of New York, and its artists include Albert Bierstadt and Frederic Church.
This founder of the Hudson River School painted the series The Course of Empire which depict the rise and fall of an imaginary city. He is more famous for his The Oxbow.

Living fossils are organisms that closely resemble species known from fossils. For 10 points each, name some:

This tree native to China dates from the Permian period, and is frequently planted in Japanese temple gardens. The single living species in its genus, it has fan-shaped leaves divided into lobes by a central notch.

This cephalopod mollusk dominated the seas 500 million years ago, before the arrival of fishes. Its shell, shaped like a logarithmic spiral, is divided into chambers; the animal itself resides in the outermost chamber.
This order of bony fishes was abundant in the Devonian period, and was thought extinct until 1938. Like lungfishes, they have lobed fins and tails, and their name comes from Greek for "hollow spine".
It's named after an Italian who discovered that electrical current could make a frog's leg jerk. For 10 points each:
Name this type of device which detects electrical current. It was the earliest type of ammeter and it experiences torque proportional to the current passing through its coil.
Named after a British scientist, this circuit consists of a galvanometer and three resistors of known value, one of which is adjustable, and is used to find the value of a fourth resistor.

The formula for a Wheatstone bridge can be derived from this set of two laws dealing with the sum of currents and the directed sum of voltages in a circuit. They are named after a German physicist who collaborated with Robert Bunsen.
His works include The Tree of Man, The Vivisector, and a work about the title explorer. For 10 points each:
Name this Australian author of Voss. He won the Nobel Prize in 1973.
White was the only winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature from this nation. Thomas Keneally, known for his Schindler's Ark, is also from this nation.
This other Australian author wrote novels such as Bliss, The Tax Inspector, and Jack Maggs but is better known for The True History of the Kelly Gang and Oscar and Lucinda.
Economic curves are cool. For 10 points each.

The Phillips curve demonstrates the inverse relationship between this quantity and unemployment, but it breaks down during stagflation. The misery index is the sum of this rate and the unemployment rate.
This curve represents income distribution. The Gini coefficient, calculated using the area between this curve and the line of perfect equality, shows the level of income inequality.
The indifference curve shows the bundles of consumption that provide equal amounts of this concept to an individual.
For 10 points each, name these mathematical functions named after Greek letters.

Although not strictly speaking a function, this uppercase letter is used to denote summation of a set of numbers, usually using an index of summation which varies between upper and lower bounds written above and beneath this letter.

This number theory function is significant because of its relation to the distribution of prime numbers. A hypothesis named after its namesake Riemann states that all of its zeroes have the real part 1/2.
While the factorial function only applies to non-negative integers, this extension of the factorial function applies to real and complex numbers.
For 10 points each, answer these things about songs titled "Around the World".

This French electronic duo's song "Around the World" has the phrase spoken 80 times in the radio edit and 144 times in the full version. The music video, directed by Michel Gondry, is intended to represent the five basic instrument sounds present in the song, in the form of robots, mummies, skeletons, synchronized swimmers, and people with prosthetic heads.

Around the World was also the title of a song by this band of their album "Californication", although more famous albums by them are their 2006 album Stadium Arcadium and their song "Under the Bridge" from the album of the same name.

This work is a collection of preludes and fugues in all 24 major and minor keys. For 10 points each:
Name this book about a specific type of instrument.

Only by lifting up a huge block of stone was he able to take his father's sandals. For 10 points each:

For 10 points each, name these musicians who died at the age of 27.

In evolutionary terms, as articulated by Ernst Mayr, this biological grouping is defined by the ability to interbreed. For 10 points each:
Name this taxon, a subdivision below genus.

Name the short collection, split into "The Garden Forking Path" and "Artifices," which contains works like "Death and the Compass" and "Pierre Menard, Author of the Quixote".

For 10 points each, name these structures in the human brain.

This lower extension of the brain connects it to the spinal cord. The vagus nerve and most other cranial nerves branch off of it, and it includes the pons and the medulla oblongata, which is responsible for autonomic functions.

B-cells are a type of these white blood cells, which also include T-cells and Natural Killer cells. The former two give rise to immunological memory and are the crucial part of the third line of defense.
